target_customer: Owners and property managers of large commercial office buildings
problem: Building systems such as heating, lighting, metering and security are siloed, so owners cannot see or manage them together or serve tenants well.
business_model: B2B software for building owners, custom per building

founders.name: Ritesh Patel
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists Patel as sole founder with no bio. Some aggregators and TechCrunch refer to him as Xitij Patel, unresolved.

founders.name: Jaimal Soni
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the YC launch blog post, not on the YC company page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Software had to integrate with existing ventilation, lighting and security systems with thousands of sensors without building hardware (YC blog 2015-03).

defensibility.rationale: Per building custom integration could create some lock-in, but with one deployment and a tiny team it was early and copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes an incumbent response. Established building automation vendors existed, but none was dated near the batch in my sources.

market_need_then: YC blog (2015-03) argued owners of large office buildings want unified control of heating, lighting, metering and security, pointing to Google buying Nest as evidence of the connected building opportunity.

branding.domain_note: buildscience.com was the listed site; it returned a 503 error during research.

identity.voice_and_tone: Describes itself as the operating system for commercial buildings

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community on the brand was found. The name matches many building science consultancies, which crowds search results.

outcome_analysis: BuildScience joined YC in Winter 2015 with a software layer to unify building systems, reportedly deployed in a one million square foot Class A office building in Toronto. No later funding, customers, acquisition or shutdown is documented in public sources I found, the YC page still lists it as active with one person, and the company site returned an error. Its trajectory after the batch is unknown, so no success or failure factors are assigned.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503. CB Insights lists a single 120K seed from YC in 2015-03 (single aggregator, standard YC deal, so not recorded as a round) and conflicts on headquarters. No dated competitor was found: a general building software search returned only current profiles. Competitors are intentionally empty. Founder name discrepancy (Ritesh vs Xitij Patel) unresolved. Completeness pass: the CB Insights seed of about 120K dated 2015-03 (YC investment) is recorded as stage other; it rests on a single database. Crunchbase shows only a seed with no amount. No press found.
